gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states what each under-$50 camera costs once the maker's own hardwire kit for parking mode is added: DDPAI's MINIPRO 2K + Hardwire Kit is $49.00, while the 70mai M310 plus 70mai's UP03 kit is $39.99 + $27.99 = $67.98.
standout_why: Compared against autoroamer.com (cited), guidespot.com (cited) and the DashCamTalk price tracker (cited). Auto Roamer says the M310 needs a separate hardwire kit and gives only a generic $15-25 kit range, with no maker kit price and no total. Guidespot gives the M310 at $27.99 and says parking mode needs hardwiring or a battery pack, with no kit price. DashCamTalk lists only tracked prices ($39.99 Amazon). None adds camera and kit, and none names a camera-plus-kit bundle that stays at or under $50. dashanddrive.com (cited) could not be opened (certificate error), so it is not ruled out; that is why this is 2 and not 3.
decides: For driving-only recording the M310 stays the pick at about $40. If the shopper wants parking mode inside the $50 budget, the only candidate I read that stays under is DDPAI MINIPRO 2K + Hardwire Kit at $49.00, a partner-store product we can link. The M310 with its required UP03 kit is $67.98, and DDPAI's N2 Front, MINI PRO 3K and MINI2X 2026 are each $59.00 with the kit. The budget line therefore has to say whether the kit is counted. This rests on prices only: I could not read DDPAI's spec pages, so the MINIPRO 2K's resolution, power backup and card limit still need a maker-page read before it gets a row.
